input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign: vLLM ROCm serving parity for the supported model set

## Description

An Investigation epic that resolves the strategy's central unknown: whether vLLM serving on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) reaches functional and performance parity with the productized CUDA builds for the platform's supported model set. The campaign stands up vLLM ROCm serving on physical AMD Instinct hardware, measures functional correctness and serving performance per model, and produces the go/no-go report that determines which models are productized. Every downstream productization decision in this strategy is gated on this campaign's outcome.

## Scope

- Secure access to dedicated physical AMD Instinct nodes (procurement or a partner-lab arrangement) — campaign setup work; the access itself is externally controlled (see Risks).
- Stand up vLLM ROCm serving on the AMD Instinct nodes using upstream-published ROCm runtime images, on a recorded driver/ROCm stack.
- Define the campaign measurement plan: the supported model set, functional test workloads, performance workloads and metrics (throughput/latency), and the CUDA-baseline comparison methodology.
- Run the campaign: per-model functional validation and performance measurement.
- Produce the go/no-go report: per-model functional results, performance versus the CUDA baseline, parity gaps (unsupported operators, driver issues, performance shortfalls), and the recommended productization scope.
- Report actionable parity gaps to the appropriate owning teams and upstream communities.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A campaign report exists that covers every model in the supported model set, with per-model functional results and per-model performance measurements against the CUDA baseline.
- The report states a per-model go/no-go recommendation with supporting data, defining the productization scope.
- The campaign methodology (hardware specification, driver and ROCm versions, model and image versions, test workloads) is recorded such that the results are reproducible.
- Identified parity gaps are documented with root cause where known, and actionable gaps are reported to the appropriate owning team or upstream community.
- Serving is exercised end-to-end through the platform's serving path (InferenceService deployment of a vLLM ROCm runtime requesting AMD GPU resources) for the models under consideration — this validates the serving stack needs no code changes for AMD GPUs.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks

- Hardware access is an availability precondition granted outside the strategy (procurement or partner-lab cadence); it is not an acceptance criterion. Delayed access slips the campaign start.
- Upstream ROCm runtime image cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream communities and constrains which runtime versions the campaign can test.

# Productize the vLLM ROCm serving runtime for campaign-cleared models

## Description

An Implementation epic that turns the validated ROCm serving capability into a productized runtime: a vLLM ROCm serving runtime image built in the midstream serving-runtimes repository, the build-pipeline support for it, and the ServingRuntime definition that makes it deployable on AMD Instinct nodes. Which models are enabled is set by the validation campaign's go/no-go outcome — this epic is gated on that resolution and its scope is rewritten to match the cleared model set.

## Scope

- Add a ROCm build variant of the vLLM serving runtime image to the midstream serving-runtimes repository, building on a released upstream ROCm base image and covering the models cleared by the validation campaign.
- Extend the repository's existing build pipeline to build and release the ROCm image variant alongside the current CUDA builds.
- Provide the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime definition that deploys the ROCm vLLM runtime with AMD GPU resource (amd.com/gpu) requests for inference.
- Verify end-to-end serving through the platform's serving path for the cleared models on AMD Instinct nodes.
- Ensure existing CUDA-based serving runtimes are unaffected by the change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The vLLM ROCm serving runtime image builds in the midstream repository and its build pipeline is green, including the repository's Konflux pipeline.
- A ServingRuntime definition deploys the ROCm vLLM runtime with amd.com/gpu resource requests, and InferenceServices using it serve the campaign-cleared models on AMD Instinct nodes.
- The set of models enabled by default matches the campaign's go/no-go scope; models that did not clear are not enabled.
- Existing CUDA-based serving runtimes and inference workloads on NVIDIA hardware show no regression from this change.
- The ROCm base image and version pinned for the productized runtime are recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks

- Gated on the validation campaign outcome: if only a subset of models clears, productize that subset; if no model clears, this epic is removed and the parity gaps are reported upstream instead of productizing.
- Upstream ROCm runtime image releases are controlled by AMD and the upstream communities and may not align with the platform's release trains; the pinned base image may need to track the closest released upstream build, which can delay availability in a given train.

# Enable PyTorch ROCm training for single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs

## Description

An Implementation epic making PyTorch training on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) a supported path: PyTorchJob workloads run single- and multi-GPU training on ROCm and are admitted through the platform's queueing system with AMD GPU quota. This epic covers the Training Operator side of that capability — the supported runtime basis for ROCm training jobs and validation of job topologies on AMD GPUs.

## Scope

- Define the supported runtime basis for PyTorch ROCm training jobs (training image, PyTorch ROCm build, and versions), building on upstream-published ROCm support.
- Enable PyTorchJob worker pods to request and run on AMD GPU resources (amd.com/gpu) in both single-GPU and multi-GPU (multi-worker) topologies.
- Validate single-GPU and multi-GPU PyTorch training jobs on ROCm on AMD Instinct nodes, including admission through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota and all-or-nothing gang semantics.
- Record the supported job shapes and any ROCm-specific constraints for multi-GPU jobs, for use by documentation and support.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob requesting amd.com/gpu completes a training run successfully on AMD Instinct nodes.
- A multi-GPU PyTorchJob completes a distributed training run successfully on AMD Instinct nodes with correct multi-worker behavior.
- Jobs are admitted through Kueue: amd.com/gpu quota is enforced and all-or-nothing admission holds for multi-GPU jobs.
- The supported PyTorch ROCm runtime basis (image and versions) is defined and recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling (job/runtime portion).

## Risks

- Validation requires physical AMD Instinct hardware; node access (procurement or partner lab) is an availability precondition granted outside the strategy and is not an acceptance criterion.
- PyTorch ROCm image releases are upstream-controlled and may not align with platform release trains.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for AMD Instinct workloads

## Description

An Implementation epic covering the Distributed Workloads (Kueue) side of AMD GPU enablement: quota and admission handling for the amd.com/gpu resource, so batch AI workloads requesting AMD Instinct accelerators are admitted, quota-accounted, and gang-scheduled like their NVIDIA counterparts.

## Scope

- Extend the queueing configuration to account for amd.com/gpu resources within the ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model.
- Define resource flavors covering AMD GPU nodes so workloads requesting amd.com/gpu are matched and admitted correctly.
- Validate quota enforcement for amd.com/gpu: admission honors quota limits, and all-or-nothing (waitForPodsReady) admission holds for multi-GPU workloads.
- Verify the AMD quota path does not disrupt existing NVIDIA GPU quota handling and admission.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Workloads requesting amd.com/gpu are admitted against ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota with correct resource accounting for AMD GPUs.
- All-or-nothing admission holds: a multi-GPU workload requesting amd.com/gpu is admitted only when its full request can be satisfied.
- Quota exhaustion behavior is verified: workloads beyond quota remain pending and are admitted when quota is released.
- Existing NVIDIA GPU quota handling and admitted workloads are unaffected.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling (quota/admission portion).

## Risks

- Quota validation on real workloads requires AMD GPU nodes; node access is an availability precondition granted outside the strategy.

# Document AMD GPU (ROCm) support: hardware, drivers, and validated models

## Description

A docs-authoring epic producing the user-facing documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement: the supported AMD hardware, the driver prerequisites, the validated model list, and the guidance users need to serve and train on AMD Instinct accelerators with the platform.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Supported AMD hardware: which AMD Instinct accelerators are supported, per the validation campaign results.
- Driver prerequisites: the required ROCm/driver stack versions for serving and training.
- Validated model list: the models cleared by the validation campaign and served by the productized vLLM ROCm runtime.
- Usage guidance for PyTorch training on ROCm: single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota.
- Limits and exclusions carried from the strategy: other accelerator families and AMD GPU sharing/partitioning are out of scope and not implied as supported.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation states the supported AMD hardware and the driver/ROCm prerequisites for both serving and training.
- Documentation states the validated model list, consistent with the campaign's go/no-go scope and what was productized.
- Documentation includes the prerequisites and usage notes for PyTorch ROCm training jobs (single- and multi-GPU through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota).
- Content is technically reviewed against the implemented capability before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. The epic's priority is P1 via the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy frontmatter priority Major → P1).
